neighbours.label: a person acting toward the writer in a personal anecdote: 'my son told me', 'a visitor sent me', 'for my students to'
fire: My sister, a nurse, told me that her shift had changed.
A reader sent me some old maps of the town.
I hate for my kids to skip their breakfast.
My neighbor, a baker, told me that the shop had closed.
A friend sent me a funny card last week.
I hate for my guests to wash the dishes.
My boss, a kind man, told me that I could leave.
A stranger sent me flowers on Friday.
quiet: Her sister, a nurse, works on a ward in town.
The shop sells some old maps of the town.
Kids in the area often skip their breakfast.
The neighbor, a baker, opens the shop at six.
The office has a funny card on the wall.
Guests in this hotel can wash their dishes.
The boss, a kind man, is on leave.
The market sells flowers on Friday.

notes: The card flags this pole broad. Probes: ' to' after 'for my students' 0.79, ' told' 0.63, ' sent' 0.40, a comma after 'reviews' 0.32; a sentence about a river 0.06.
